data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not substantive but procedural: Report 1 returned inconclusive due to LLM API failures (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) on PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, while Report 2 successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. Report 3 is advisory-only with a tool error. There is no actual disagreement about security findings—only about whether the audit could complete.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen): LLM API failed with HTTP 400 on PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO - the two most critical files for security audit
Report 3 (openrouter/free): LLM returned error payload, only attempted PKGBUILD review and failed
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) on critical files like PKGBUILD should trigger automatic retry or escalation rather than marking the entire audit inconclusive
When multiple reports exist and one has complete coverage with sound reasoning while others have tool errors, the complete report should be weighted more heavily
Advisory reports with tool errors should be clearly distinguished from substantive inconclusive verdicts in the disagreement detection logic
